title: The Ultimate Hype Man and a Fast Start
paragraphs: § John the Baptizer
The good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, starts right here.

It began exactly how the ancient prophet Isaiah said it would: "Watch closely—I'm sending my messenger ahead of you to clear the path. He's going to be a voice shouting in the desert, telling everyone to get ready for the Lord."
That messenger was John the Baptist. He showed up in the desert with a bold message: "Turn your life around, get baptized, and God will forgive your sins."
People from all over Judea and Jerusalem flocked out to the wilderness to see John. They confessed their sins and got baptized by him in the Jordan River.
John wore a camel-hair coat with a leather belt around his waist, and he lived on locusts and wild honey.

John preached, "The real action comes next. The star of this drama is coming after me — I'm just a stagehand compared to him. He's going to change your life. I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit, changing you from the inside out."

Jesus traveled from Nazareth to the Jordan River, and John baptized him. The second Jesus came up out of the water, the sky ripped open, and the Holy Spirit came down on him like a dove. A voice from heaven boomed: "You are my Son, and I love you. I am incredibly proud of you."
§ God's Kingdom Is Here

Immediately after that, the Spirit pushed Jesus out into the harsh wilderness. He was out there for forty days, surrounded by wild animals, getting completely tested and tempted by Satan. But angels stepped in and took care of him.
After John got arrested, Jesus went to the Galilee region and started preaching: "Time's up! God's kingdom is right here. Change your ways and believe the good news!"

Walking down the beach, Jesus saw two brothers, Simon (Peter) and Andrew, throwing their fishing nets into the water. Fishing was their everyday job. Jesus called out, "Come follow me! I'll teach you how to fish for actual people instead of perch and bass." They dropped their nets on the spot and followed him. A little further down, he saw James and John, the sons of Zebedee, fixing nets in their boat. He called them too, and right away they left their dad Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and joined the crew.
§ Confident Teaching

They went into the town of Capernaum. On the Sabbath (the day of rest), Jesus went to the local gathering place and started teaching. People were mind-blown because he spoke with absolute authority, not like their boring religious teachers.
Suddenly, a guy possessed by an evil spirit started screaming at him: "What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth?! Did you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!"
Jesus didn't flinch. "Be quiet and get out of him!" he commanded. The evil spirit violently threw the man into a spasm, shrieked, and left.

Everyone there was spellbound, buzzing with curiosity. "What's going on? A new teaching—and it actually works! He shuts up unclean spirits and tells them to get lost!" News about Jesus spread like wildfire through the whole region of Galilee.

After that, Jesus went to Simon and Andrew's house, with James and John along. Simon's mother-in-law was in bed, burning up with fever. They told Jesus about her. He went to her, took her hand, and helped her up—and the fever left her instantly. She got right up and started making dinner for them. That evening, after sunset, the whole town crowded at the door, bringing everyone who was sick or tormented by evil spirits. Jesus healed their sick bodies and freed their troubled minds. The demons knew exactly who he was, so he shut them up—no talking.
§ The Leper
Way before sunrise, Jesus got up and slipped away to a quiet spot to pray. Simon and the others went looking for him. When they finally found him, they said, "Everyone's looking for you!"
Jesus said, "Let's head to the nearby villages. I need to preach there too—that's exactly why I came."
So he traveled all through Galilee, preaching in their meeting places and driving out demons.

Later, a guy covered in leprosy fell on his knees and begged Jesus, "If you want to, you can heal me." Jesus felt deep pity for the guy, reached out, and actually touched him. "I want to," Jesus said. "Be healed." Instantly, the leprosy vanished, and his skin was smooth and healthy again.

Jesus sent him away with a strong warning: "Don't tell anyone about this. Just go, show yourself to the priest, and offer what Moses commanded for your cleansing, as a testimony to them." But the guy went out and started talking freely, spreading the news everywhere. As a result, Jesus couldn't enter towns openly anymore—he had to stay out in lonely places. But people still came to him from everywhere.

title: Ripping Off the Roof and Breaking the Rules
paragraphs: § A Paraplegic
A few days later, Jesus was back in Capernaum. Word got out, and the house he was in got packed so tight nobody could even get through the front door. He was teaching the Word.

Four guys brought a paralyzed man on a stretcher, but they couldn't get past the crowd. So, they climbed up onto the roof, literally ripped a hole in it, and lowered him down on his stretcher right in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw how massive their faith was, he looked at the paralyzed guy and said, "Son, your sins are forgiven."
Some stuck-up religious experts sitting right there started thinking, "This is blasphemy! Who does this guy think he is? Only God can forgive sins."

Jesus knew exactly what they were thinking. He said, "Why are you guys so skeptical? What's easier to say: 'Your sins are forgiven' or 'Get up and walk'? Just to prove the Son of Man has the authority to forgive sins here on earth..." He turned to the paralyzed guy: "Get up, grab your mat, and go home."
The guy stood right up, grabbed his mat, and walked out while everyone stared in total shock, praising God. They said, "We've never seen anything like this!"
§ The Tax Collector
Jesus went back out to the lakeshore. A huge crowd gathered around him, and he taught them.
Later, Jesus saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at his tax booth. Jesus said, "Follow me," and Levi got up and followed him.

Levi threw a massive dinner party at his house with Jesus, his disciples, and a ton of other shady tax collectors and "sinners." Crazy as it sounds, quite a few of them had already become his followers. The religion scholars and Pharisees saw this and asked his disciples, "Why does he eat with outcasts?"
Jesus overheard them and dropped this logic: "Healthy people don't need a doctor—sick people do. I didn't come to invite the rule-followers; I came to invite the misfits."
§ Feasting or Fasting?
John's disciples and the Pharisees fasted on the regular. So some people came to Jesus and demanded, "John's disciples and the Pharisees do fasting training—why don't your disciples?"

Jesus said, "At a wedding party, don't people eat, drink, and have a blast? How can they fast while the groom is right there with them? Sure, a day might come when they'll have to tighten their belts, but not now. While the groom is here, it's party time. Who'd pour cold water on this joyful mood? This is exactly what God's kingdom arriving looks like!"

He kept going: "Nobody rips a piece of new cloth to patch old clothes—the patch just tears the hole even bigger. And nobody pours new wine into old wineskins—they'd burst and you'd lose both the wine and the skins. New wine goes into new wineskins."

One Sabbath day, Jesus and his guys were walking through a wheat field. The disciples pulled off some heads of grain as they made their way through. The Pharisees threw a fit: "Look! They are breaking the Sabbath rules!"

Jesus shut them down: "Did you ever read what King David did when his guys were starving? He walked right into the sanctuary and ate the holy bread off the altar—with Chief Priest Abiathar standing right there watching! That bread was only for priests, but David shared it with his companions too. Listen to me: The Sabbath was made to help people; people weren't made to be slaves to the Sabbath. The Son of Man doesn't take orders from the Sabbath—he's in charge of it!"

title: The Starting Lineup and Unforgivable Trash Talk
paragraphs: § Doing Good on the Sabbath

Jesus went back to the meeting place, and there was a guy there with a crippled, shriveled hand. The Pharisees watched Jesus like hawks, waiting to see if he would heal the guy on the Sabbath so they could accuse him of breaking the Sabbath.

Jesus told the crippled man, "Stand up right here in the middle." Then Jesus asked the people, "Is it legal to do good on the Sabbath, or to do evil? To save a life, or kill?" They sat there in dead silence.
Jesus looked them in the eye, one after another, absolutely furious at how stubborn and cold they were. He told the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man did, and it was perfectly healed.
The Pharisees immediately stormed out and held a secret meeting with Herod's followers to figure out how to ruin Jesus.
§ The Twelve Apostles

Jesus went off with his disciples to the sea to get away. But the crowds following him were getting dangerously huge. People from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, across the Jordan, and around Tyre and Sidon had heard the reports and came to see for themselves. He had healed so many people that everyone who had something wrong was pushing and shoving just to touch him. He had to have his disciples keep a small boat ready so he wouldn't get trampled by the crowd.
Whenever the evil spirits saw Jesus, they'd fall down right in front of him and scream, "You are the Son of God!" But Jesus shut them down hard—he warned them not to tell anyone who he was.

Jesus hiked up a mountain and called up the specific guys he wanted on his core team. He appointed twelve of them to be his official "apostles" (messengers). The plan was that they would be with him, and he would send them out to proclaim the Word and give them authority to banish demons. They were: Simon—Jesus later named him Peter, meaning "Rock"; James son of Zebedee and his brother John—Jesus nicknamed the brothers Boanerges, meaning "Sons of Thunder"; Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot (who betrayed him).
§ Satan Fighting Satan?

Jesus went home, but the crowd was so crazy he and his guys couldn't even eat. The people closest to him heard what was going on and came to take charge of him, by force if necessary—they thought he was losing it.

The religious experts from Jerusalem showed up and started a rumor: "He's possessed by Beelzebul (Satan). He's only kicking out demons because he's getting his power from the boss of the demons — it's all devil tricks to impress people with spiritual power."

Jesus called them over and exposed how clueless that logic was: "Does it make sense to send a devil to catch a devil—to use Satan to get rid of Satan? A constantly squabbling family disintegrates. If Satan were fighting Satan, there soon wouldn't be any Satan left. And do you think you can walk into the house of a strong, wide-awake man in broad daylight and walk off with his stuff unless you tie him up first? Tie him up, though, and you can clean him out."

Then he gave them a hardcore warning: "Listen to this carefully — I'm warning you. There's nothing done or said that can't be forgiven. But if you keep slandering God's Holy Spirit, you're turning your back on the very One who forgives. It's like sawing off the branch you're sitting on — you're cutting off your own connection to the One who forgives, all by yourself." He gave them this warning because they were accusing him of being in league with Evil.
§ Jesus' Mother and Brothers

Then Jesus' mother and brothers showed up. They stood outside and sent someone in to tell Jesus they needed to talk. Jesus was surrounded by a crowd when he heard, "Your mother and brothers and sisters are outside looking for you."

Jesus answered, "Who do you think my mother and brothers are?" Then he looked around at everyone sitting in a circle and said, "My mother and brothers are right here in front of you. Obedience runs thicker than blood. Anyone who lives by God's will—that's my brother, my sister, my mother."

title: Stories in the Dirt and a Wild Storm
paragraphs: § The Story of the Scattered Seed
Jesus went back to teach by the lake. The crowd was so massive he had to get into a boat and teach from the water. He taught them using "parables" (stories with hidden meanings).
"Listen up! What do you make of this? A farmer went out to plant seeds.
Some fell on the walking path, and birds ate them immediately.
Some fell on gravel. They sprouted fast but burned up in the sun because they had no roots.
Some fell in the weeds, which choked the plants so they couldn't produce anything.
But some fell in good, rich dirt and came up with a flourish, producing a harvest way beyond the farmer's wildest dreams!"
"Are you listening to this? Really listening?"

When they were alone, the Twelve and the others around him asked about the parables. He told them, "You guys get the inside scoop on God's kingdom—you know how it works. But for everyone else, I have to use stories. It gets them ready, nudges them toward actually getting it. These are people whose eyes are open but they don't see a thing, whose ears are open but they don't hear a word. They won't turn around, and they won't accept forgiveness."
Then he said, "Do you get how this story works? All my stories work this way."

"Here's what it means. The farmer plants the Word. Some people are like the seed scattered on the hard path. They hear the Word, and boom—Satan swoops in and snatches away what was just planted in them."

"Some are like the seed in the gravel. They hear the Word and get super pumped right away. But it's shallow—there's no root. As soon as the emotions wear off and trouble or pushback comes because of the Word, they bail, with nothing to show for it."

"The seed in the weeds? That's people who hear the kingdom news but get totally overwhelmed—so much to do, so much they want, so many worries. The stress chokes out what they heard, and nothing comes of it."
"But the seed in the good soil? That's people who hear the Word, hold onto it for real, and produce a harvest way beyond their wildest dreams."
§ Giving, Not Getting

Jesus kept teaching: "Who brings a lamp just to hide it under a bowl or a bed? Obviously you put it on a table or a shelf. We're not trying to keep secrets—we're trying to broadcast them. Nothing stays hidden; everything gets exposed."
"Are you actually listening? Like, really listening?"

"Listen carefully to what I'm saying—and watch out for the slick advice that tells you how to get ahead in life on your own. Giving, not getting, is the way. Generosity creates generosity. Stinginess just makes you poor."
§ Never Without a Story

Then Jesus said, "God's kingdom is like this. A guy throws seed on a field, then goes to bed and totally forgets about it. The seed sprouts and grows—he has no idea how it happens. The ground does everything by itself: first a green stem pops up, then a bud, then ripe grain. When the grain is fully ready, he harvests. It's harvest time!"

Jesus also said: "What is God's kingdom like? What kind of story can we use? It's like an acorn. When it lands on the ground it's tiny as seeds go, but once it's planted it grows into a huge oak tree with thick branches. Eagles nest in it."

Jesus always taught the crowds with stories like these, matching the stories to what they could actually handle — He never taught them without a story. But when it was just Him and His disciples, He broke it all down, untangling every knot and answering everything.
§ The Wind Ran Out of Breath
When evening came, Jesus told his crew, "Let's cross to the other side of the lake." They left the crowd behind.
They took him in the boat just as he was. A few other little boats followed along too.

While they were sailing, a sudden hurricane whipped up. The waves were so massive they were crashing into the boat, and it was starting to sink. Jesus was in the back of the boat, fast asleep on a cushion.
The disciples woke him up, screaming in a panic, "Teacher! Don't you care that we are about to drown?!"
Jesus woke up, told the wind to "Quiet down," and told the waves to "Chill out." Immediately, the wind stopped, and the lake went dead calm.
He turned on his crew and reprimanded them: "Why are you such cowards? Do you still not have any faith?"
The disciples were in absolute awe, totally staggered. They whispered to each other, "Who is this guy?! Even the wind and the water take orders from him!"

title: The Graveyard Zombie and the Dead Girl
paragraphs: § The Madman

They landed on the other side of the lake in the country of the Gerasenes. The moment Jesus stepped out of the boat, a madman from the cemetery came up to him. He lived there among the tombs and graves. No one could restrain him—he couldn't be chained, couldn't be tied down. He had been tied up many times with chains and ropes, but he broke the chains and snapped the ropes. No one was strong enough to tame him. Night and day he roamed through the graves and the hills, screaming out and slashing himself with sharp stones.

When he saw Jesus a long way off, he ran and bowed in worship before him—then howled in protest, "What business do you have, Jesus, Son of the High God, messing with me? I swear to God, don't give me a hard time!" (Jesus had just commanded the tormenting evil spirit, "Out! Get out of the man!")
Jesus asked him, "Tell me your name." The demon replied, "My name is Mob—I'm a rioting mob." Then he desperately begged Jesus not to banish them from the country.

A large herd of pigs was grazing and rooting on a nearby hill. The demons begged him, "Send us to the pigs so we can live in them." Jesus gave the order. But it was even worse for the pigs than for the man. Crazed, they stampeded over a cliff into the sea and drowned.

Those tending the pigs, scared to death, bolted and told their story in town and country. Everyone wanted to see what had happened. They came up to Jesus and saw the madman sitting there wearing decent clothes and making sense, no longer a walking madhouse of a man.

Those who had seen it told the others what had happened to the demon-possessed man and the pigs. At first they were in awe—and then they were upset, upset over the drowned pigs. They demanded that Jesus leave and not come back.

As Jesus was getting into the boat, the demon-delivered man begged to go along, but he wouldn't let him. Jesus said, "Go home to your own people. Tell them your story—what the Master did, how he had mercy on you." The man went back and began to preach in the Ten Towns area about what Jesus had done for him. He was the talk of the town.
§ A Risk of Faith

After Jesus crossed over by boat, a large crowd met him at the seaside. One of the meeting-place leaders named Jairus came. When he saw Jesus, he fell to his knees, beside himself as he begged, "My dear daughter is at death's door. Come and lay hands on her so she will get well and live." Jesus went with him, the whole crowd tagging along, pushing and jostling him.

A woman who had suffered a condition of hemorrhaging for twelve years—a long succession of physicians had treated her, and treated her badly, taking all her money and leaving her worse off than before—had heard about Jesus. She slipped in from behind and touched his robe. She was thinking to herself, "If I can put a finger on his robe, I can get well." The moment she did it, the flow of blood dried up. She could feel the change and knew her plague was over and done with.
At the same moment, Jesus felt energy discharging from him. He turned around to the crowd and asked, "Who touched my robe?"
His disciples said, "What are you talking about? With this crowd pushing and jostling you, you're asking, 'Who touched me?' Dozens have touched you!"

But he went on asking, looking around to see who had done it. The woman, knowing what had happened, knowing she was the one, stepped up in fear and trembling, knelt before him, and gave him the whole story.
Jesus said to her, "Daughter, you took a risk of faith, and now you're healed and whole. Live well, live blessed! Be healed of your plague."
While he was still talking, some people came from the leader's house and told him, "Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?"
Jesus overheard what they were talking about and said to the leader, "Don't listen to them; just trust me."

He permitted no one to go in with him except Peter, James, and John. They entered the leader's house and pushed their way through the gossips looking for a story and neighbors bringing in casseroles. Jesus was abrupt: "Why all this busybody grief and gossip? This child isn't dead; she's sleeping." Provoked to sarcasm, they told him he didn't know what he was talking about.

But when he had sent them all out, he took the child's father and mother, along with his companions, and entered the child's room. He clasped the girl's hand and said, "Talitha koum," which means, "Little girl, get up." At that, she was up and walking around! This girl was twelve years of age. They, of course, were all beside themselves with joy. He gave them strict orders that no one was to know what had taken place in that room. Then he said, "Give her something to eat."

title: Hometown Rejection, a Gruesome Party, and Defying Gravity
paragraphs: § Just a Carpenter

Jesus headed back to his hometown, and his crew (disciples) went with him. On the Sabbath, he gave a talk in the synagogue (their meeting place for worship and teaching). He totally crushed it, blowing everyone away. They were like, "Whoa, where did this guy get all this? We had no clue he was this amazing! How'd he get so smart all of a sudden, and able to do all these powerful things?"

But then, in the very next breath, they started tearing him down. "Isn't this just the carpenter? Mary's son? We've known him since he was a little kid! We know his brothers, James, Justus, Jude, and Simon, and his sisters. Who does he think he is, anyway?" They completely stumbled over the limited stuff they thought they knew about him, and that was it. They couldn't move past it.

Jesus told them, "A prophet doesn't get much respect in his hometown, among his own relatives, or even on the streets where he grew up." Honestly, Jesus couldn't really do much there—he just laid hands on a few sick people and healed them, and that was it. He was genuinely shocked by how stubborn and closed-minded they were. So, he left and went around to the other villages, teaching.
§ The Twelve

Jesus called the twelve disciples to him and sent them out in pairs. He gave them the authority and power to deal with evil opposition (demons and spiritual forces). He sent them off with these instructions:
"Don't think you need a lot of extra gear for this. You guys are the gear! No special fundraising appeals. Keep it simple."
"And no luxury inns. Find a modest place and be cool with staying there until you move on."
"If you're not welcomed, or if people don't listen to you, just quietly leave. Don't make a big scene. Just shrug it off and keep moving."

So, they hit the road. They preached with a joyful urgency that life could be totally different and amazing. They were casting out demons left and right, and they brought healing to the sick, anointing their bodies with oil (a traditional practice for healing) and restoring their spirits.
§ The Death of John
King Herod heard about all this, because by now, Jesus's name was on everyone's lips. Herod said, "This has to be John the Baptizer, back from the dead—that's why he's able to work miracles!"
Others were saying, "No, it's Elijah (a famous prophet from the Old Testament)." Still others were like, "He's a prophet, just like one of those prophets from way back when."
But Herod wouldn't budge from his idea: "It's John, for sure. I'm the one who had his head cut off, and now he's back, alive."

Herod was the one who had ordered John's arrest, put him in chains, and thrown him in prison. This was all because of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, who was constantly nagging him. John had really ticked Herod off by calling out his relationship with Herodias as "adultery" (being unfaithful in marriage).

Herodias was absolutely fuming with hate and wanted to kill John, but she didn't dare because Herod was actually kind of in awe of John. He was convinced John was a holy man and gave him special treatment. Whenever he listened to John, he felt totally miserable with guilt—and yet, he couldn't stay away. Something about John kept pulling him back.

But then, a really important (and bad) day arrived when Herod threw a huge birthday party, inviting all the important officials and high-society people in Galilee. Herodias's daughter came into the banquet hall and danced for all the guests. She totally charmed Herod and everyone else.
The king said to the girl, "Ask me for anything. I'll give you whatever you want." Getting totally carried away, he kept going, "I swear, I'll even split my kingdom with you if you ask for it!"
She went back to her mom and asked, "What should I ask for?" Her mom immediately replied, "Ask for the head of John the Baptizer."
Super excited, she ran back to the king and said, "I want the head of John the Baptizer served up on a platter. And I want it right now!"

That sobered the king up really fast. But he didn't want to look bad in front of his guests, so he totally caved in and let her have her wish. The king sent the executioner off to the prison with orders to bring back John's head. The executioner went, cut off John's head, brought it back on a platter, and presented it to the girl, who then gave it to her mother. When John's disciples heard about this, they came, got the body, and gave it a respectful burial.
§ Supper for Five Thousand

The apostles then met back up with Jesus and reported on everything they had done and taught. Jesus said, "Come off by yourselves; let's take a break and get a little rest." This was because people were constantly coming and going, so much so that they didn't even have time to eat.

So they got into a boat and went off to a remote place by themselves. But someone saw them going, and the word spread fast. People from all the towns nearby started running on foot and got there ahead of them.
When Jesus arrived, he saw this massive crowd. Looking at them, his heart just broke—they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he immediately started teaching them.

When his disciples thought this had gone on long enough—it was getting pretty late in the day—they interrupted: "We're way out in the country here, and it's super late. Say a blessing and send these folks off so they can go get some dinner."
Jesus said, "You do it. You fix dinner for them."
They replied, "Are you serious? You want us to go spend a fortune (a huge amount of money) on food for their dinner?"
But he was totally serious. "How many loaves of bread do you have? Go check." That didn't take long. "Five," they said, "plus two fish."

Jesus had them all sit down in groups of fifty or a hundred—they looked like a colorful patchwork quilt of wildflowers spread out on the green grass! He took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven in prayer, blessed them, broke them, and gave the bread to the disciples, who then passed it out to the people. He did the same with the fish. Everyone ate until they were completely full. The disciples gathered twelve baskets of leftovers. More than five thousand people were at that dinner.
§ Walking on the Sea

As soon as the meal was finished, Jesus insisted that the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead across to Bethsaida while he dismissed the crowd. After sending everyone off, he climbed a mountain to pray.

Late at night, the boat was far out at sea, and Jesus was still by himself on land. He could see his men struggling with the oars because the wind had picked up against them. At about four o'clock in the morning, Jesus came toward them, walking on the sea. He actually intended to walk right past them.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost and screamed, scared to death.

Jesus was quick to comfort them: "Courage! It's me. Don't be afraid." As soon as he climbed into the boat, the wind completely died down. They were totally stunned, shaking their heads, wondering what in the world was going on. They hadn't really understood what he had done at the supper. None of this had truly sunk into their hearts yet.

They finally beached the boat at Gennesaret and tied up at the landing. As soon as they got out of the boat, word got around super fast. People ran all over the place, bringing their sick on stretchers to wherever they heard he was. Wherever he went, whether it was a village, town, or country crossroads, they brought their sick to the marketplace and begged him just to let them touch the edge of his coat—that's all they asked. And everyone who touched him became well.

title: Fake Rules and a Savage Mom
paragraphs: § The Source of Your Pollution

Some Pharisees and religious scholars, who had traveled all the way from Jerusalem, showed up and gathered around Jesus. They immediately noticed that some of Jesus’s disciples weren't following the traditional rules about washing their hands before eating. See, the Pharisees—and most Jewish people back then—would never, ever eat a meal without doing a whole ritual hand-washing. They'd scrub super hard, especially if they’d just come from the market, and don't even get me started on how much they'd scrub their jugs, pots, and pans too!
The Pharisees and those religious scholars were like, "Seriously, why do your disciples just ignore the rules? Why are they eating without washing their hands first?"
Jesus shot back, "Isaiah totally nailed it when he talked about fakes like you guys. He hit the bull's-eye!"

"These people act like they're saying all the right things, but their hearts aren't really in it. They pretend to worship me, but they don't actually mean it. They just use me as an excuse to teach whatever they feel like, ditching God's actual commands and just following whatever new trends are popular."
He kept going, "Oh, great job, you guys! You get rid of God's command just so you don't have to deal with the inconvenience of following your own religious trends!"
"Moses said, ‘Respect your father and mother,’ and also, ‘Anyone who curses their father or mother should be put to death.’"

"But you guys totally wiggle out of that! You say it's perfectly fine to tell your mom or dad, ‘Hey, what I owed you? I've already given it as a gift to God!’ (This was a way to dedicate money or property to God, making it unavailable for family support)."

"By doing that, you completely get out of your responsibility to your father or mother. You basically erase God’s actual Word and scribble in your own random ideas instead. And honestly, you do a lot of stuff like this!"
Jesus then called the crowd back together and said, "Listen up, everyone—really pay attention to this."
"It's not what you eat or swallow that makes your life messed up; it's what comes *out* of you—that's the real pollution."
When Jesus got back home after being with the crowd, his disciples were like, "Uh, we don't really get it. Can you explain it in plain language?"
Jesus responded, "Are you guys seriously being intentionally dense? Don't you see that what you eat can't actually make you dirty or bad?"

"It doesn't go into your heart, only your stomach. Then it just moves through your digestive system and eventually gets flushed out." (And with that, Jesus basically ended all arguments about what foods were okay to eat; he was saying all foods are fine).

He continued, "No, it's what comes *out* of a person that pollutes them: nasty words, messed-up desires, stealing, murder, cheating on your spouse, greed, total nastiness, tricky dealings, wild parties, mean looks, gossiping, being super arrogant, and just plain foolishness—all these ugly things are like vomit from the heart. *That's* where your real pollution comes from."
From there, Jesus headed towards the area of Tyre. He went into a house, hoping no one would find him, but he couldn't stay hidden for long.
He had barely stepped inside when a woman, whose daughter was really struggling with a demon, heard where he was. She came right away and knelt at his feet, desperately begging for help.
This woman was Greek, born in Syro-Phoenicia (a Gentile, not Jewish). She asked him to heal her daughter.
Jesus said to her, "Hold on, take your turn. The children get fed first. If there's any food left over, then the dogs get it."
She quickly replied, "Of course, Master. But don't even the dogs under the table get to eat the scraps that the children drop?"
Jesus was really impressed. "You're right! Go on home! Your daughter isn't troubled anymore. The demonic problem is gone."
She went home and found her daughter peacefully lying on the bed, totally calm, with the torment completely gone for good.
After that, Jesus left the region of Tyre, went through Sidon, then back to the Sea of Galilee, and over to the area known as the Ten Towns (Decapolis).
Some people brought a man who couldn't hear or speak and asked Jesus to lay his hand on him to heal him.

Jesus took the man away from the crowd by himself. He put his fingers in the man's ears and then spit on the man's tongue. Then Jesus looked up to heaven in prayer, let out a deep groan, and commanded, "Ephphatha!"—which means, "Open up!"
And just like that, it happened. The man's hearing was perfectly clear, and he could speak plainly—just like that, instantly.
Jesus told everyone to keep it quiet, but they just talked about it even more, completely overwhelmed with excitement.
"He's done everything so well! He makes the deaf hear and the mute speak!" they exclaimed.

title: Blind Eyes and a Hard Reality Check
paragraphs: § A Meal for Four Thousand

Around this time, Jesus found himself with another huge, hungry crowd on his hands. He called his disciples over and said, "I feel so bad for this crowd. They've been hanging out with me for three days straight, and now they don't have anything left to eat. If I send them home hungry, they'll totally pass out on the way home—some of them have come a really long distance."
His disciples were like, "Uh, what do you want us to do about it? Where are we gonna buy food out here in the middle of nowhere?"
Jesus asked, "How much bread do you have?" They told him, "Seven loaves."

So Jesus told everyone to chill out and sit down on the ground. After a quick prayer of thanks, he took the seven loaves of bread, broke them up, and gave them to his disciples so they could distribute them to the crowd. They also had a few small fish. He blessed the fish too and told his disciples to hand those out as well.

The crowd ate until they were stuffed. They even collected seven baskets of leftovers! Over four thousand people had eaten that day. Then he sent them all home. Jesus himself immediately got into the boat with his disciples and headed off for Dalmanoutha.

When they arrived, the Pharisees showed up and immediately started grilling him, demanding he prove himself, really putting him on the spot. Jesus, clearly annoyed, said, "Why does this generation keep begging for some kind of miraculous proof? Seriously, if I have anything to say about it, you won't get even the slightest hint of a guarantee."
§ Contaminating Yeast

He then left them, got back in the boat, and headed for the other side of the lake. But the disciples totally spaced on packing lunch. Except for one lonely loaf of bread, there wasn't a single crumb in the whole boat. Jesus warned them, "Listen up! Be super careful. Keep a sharp eye out for the contaminating yeast of the Pharisees and Herod's followers."

Meanwhile, the disciples were low-key arguing with each other because they'd forgotten to bring bread. Jesus overheard and said, "Why are you guys fussing just because you forgot bread? Don't you see the point of all this? Are you seriously not getting it yet? Remember the five loaves I broke for the five thousand people? How many baskets of leftovers did you pick up that time?"
They said, "Twelve."
"And the seven loaves for the four thousand—how many bags full of leftovers did you get then?" Jesus asked.
"Seven," they replied.
He said, "So, do you still not get it?"

They arrived at Bethsaida. Some people brought a man who couldn't see and begged Jesus to give him a healing touch. Taking the man by the hand, Jesus led him outside the village. He put some spit in the man's eyes, laid his hands on him, and asked, "Do you see anything?"

The man looked up. "I see men. They look like walking trees," he said. So Jesus laid his hands on the man's eyes again. The man looked hard and suddenly realized he had perfect sight; he could see everything super clearly, in bright, twenty-twenty focus. Jesus sent him straight home, telling him, "Don't even go back into the village."
§ The Messiah
Jesus and his disciples headed out for the villages around Caesarea Philippi. As they walked, he asked them, "Who do people say I am?"
They said, "Some say 'John the Baptizer.' Others say 'Elijah.' Still others say 'one of the prophets.'"
He then asked, "And you guys—what are *you* saying about me? Who am I, really?"
Peter immediately answered, "You are the Christ, the Messiah."

Jesus warned them to keep it on the down-low, not to breathe a word of it to anyone. He then started explaining things to them: "It's necessary that the Son of Man go through a really tough time of suffering, be tried and found guilty by the elders, high priests, and religion scholars. He'll be killed, and then after three days, he'll rise up alive." He said this simply and clearly so they couldn't miss it.

But Peter grabbed him in protest. Turning and seeing his disciples wavering, wondering what to believe, Jesus confronted Peter. "Peter, get out of my way! Satan, get lost! You have no idea how God works."

Calling the crowd to join his disciples, he said, "Anyone who wants to come with me has to let me lead. You're not in the driver's seat; I am. Don't run from suffering; embrace it. Follow me and I'll show you how. Trying to help yourself is no help at all. Self-sacrifice is the way, my way, to truly saving yourself, your real self. What good would it do to get absolutely everything you want but lose you, the real you? What could you ever trade your soul for?"

"If any of you are embarrassed over me and the way I'm leading you when you're around your wishy-washy and distracted friends, know that you'll be an even greater embarrassment to the Son of Man when he arrives in all the awesome splendor of God, his Father, with an army of the holy angels."

title: The Mountain Transformation and Real Greatness
paragraphs: § The Messiah

Jesus really emphasized his point, saying, "Listen, this isn't just some future dream. Some of you standing right here are actually going to see it happen, see God's kingdom arrive for real, with all its power."
§ In a Light-Radiant Cloud

Sure enough, six days later, three of them totally saw it. Jesus took Peter, James, and John and hiked them up a super tall mountain. Right before their eyes, his whole appearance transformed from the inside out. His clothes were super bright, practically glowing white—like no laundry detergent could ever get them that white. Then, Elijah and Moses just showed up, in deep conversation with Jesus.

Peter cut in, "Teacher, this is an awesome moment! Let's build three little shelters (like tents or booths)—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." He just said it without even thinking, because they were all totally blown away by what they were seeing.
Just then, a super bright, glowing cloud covered them, and then a voice boomed from inside the cloud: "This is my Son, whom I love so much. Listen to him!"
The next minute, the disciples were looking around, rubbing their eyes, and all they saw was Jesus, just Jesus.

As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus made them promise to keep it a secret. "Don't tell a single soul what you saw. After the Son of Man rises from the dead, then you're free to talk." That really puzzled them, and they wondered what on earth "rising from the dead" even meant.
Meanwhile, they were asking, "Why do the religious scholars (the experts in Jewish law) say that Elijah has to come first?"

Jesus replied, "Elijah does come first and gets everything ready for the Son of Man to arrive. But they treated this Elijah like dirt, much like they will treat the Son of Man, who, according to the Scriptures, will suffer terribly and be treated with total disrespect."
§ There Are No Ifs

When they got back down the mountain to the other disciples, they saw a huge crowd around them, and the religious scholars were grilling them with questions. As soon as the people in the crowd saw Jesus, they got super excited and ran to greet him. Jesus asked, "What's going on? Why all the chaos?"

A man from the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought my son to you. He can't speak because a demon has made him mute. Whenever it grabs him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and goes stiff as a board. I asked your disciples, hoping they could get rid of it, but they couldn't."

Jesus said, "Seriously, what's up with this generation? You have no sense of God! How many times do I have to explain these things? How much longer do I have to put up with this? Bring the boy here." So they brought him. When the demon saw Jesus, it immediately threw the boy into a seizure, making him writhe on the ground and foam at the mouth.
Jesus asked the boy's father, "How long has this been happening?"

"Ever since he was a little kid," the father answered. "Many times it throws him into fire or into the river to try and kill him. If you can do anything, please do it. Have some compassion and help us!"
Jesus responded, "'If'? There are no 'ifs' for people who believe. Anything can happen!"
No sooner had Jesus said that than the father cried out, "Then I believe! Help me with my doubts!"

Seeing that the crowd was growing fast, Jesus gave the evil spirit its orders: "You spirit that keeps him from speaking and hearing, I command you—Get out of him, and stay out!" The spirit screamed and thrashed around a lot, then it left. The boy was so pale he looked like a corpse, so people started saying, "He's dead."
But Jesus took his hand and helped him up. The boy stood up.
After they arrived back home, his disciples cornered Jesus and asked, "Why couldn't we get that demon out?"
He answered, "There's no way to get rid of this kind of demon except by prayer."

Leaving there, they traveled through Galilee. Jesus didn't want anyone to know where they were because he wanted to teach his disciples. He told them, "The Son of Man is about to be betrayed to people who want nothing to do with God. They will murder him. But three days after his murder, he will rise, alive."
They didn't really understand what he was talking about, but they were too scared to ask him about it.
§ So You Want First Place?
They arrived in Capernaum. When he was safely at home, he asked them, "What were you guys arguing about on the road?"
The silence was deafening—they had been arguing with each other over who among them was the greatest.
He sat down and called the Twelve (his main disciples) over. "So you want first place? Then you need to take the last place. Be the servant of everyone."

He put a child in the middle of the room. Then, holding the little one in his arms, he said, "Whoever welcomes one of these children just like I do, welcomes me. And even more than me—they welcome God who sent me."
John spoke up, "Teacher, we saw a guy using your name to cast out demons, and we stopped him because he wasn't part of our group."

Jesus wasn't pleased. "Don't stop him. No one can use my name to do something good and powerful, and then immediately turn around and trash me. If he's not against us, he's on our side. Seriously, anyone who just gives you a cup of water in my name is with us. You can count on God noticing that."

"On the other hand, if you cause one of these simple, childlike believers to stumble, bullying them or taking advantage of their innocent trust, you'll soon wish you hadn't. You'd be better off dropped in the middle of the lake with a huge stone (a millstone) tied around your neck."

"If your hand or your foot gets in God's way, chop it off and throw it away! You're better off maimed or lame and alive than having two hands and two feet and ending up godless in a furnace of eternal fire. And if your eye distracts you from God, pull it out and throw it away! You're better off one-eyed and alive than having perfect vision and ending up in the fire of hell."
"Everyone's going through a refining fire sooner or later, but you'll be well-preserved, protected from the eternal flames. Be preservatives yourselves. Preserve the peace."

title: Rich Guys, Blind Guys, and Boss Ambitions
paragraphs: § Divorce
From there, Jesus headed to the Judea area, across the Jordan River. As usual, a huge crowd of people tagged along, and just like always, he taught them.
Some Pharisees showed up, totally planning to give him a hard time. They asked, "Is it even legal for a guy to divorce his wife?"
Jesus shot back, "What did Moses tell you to do about it?"
They replied, "Moses said it was okay to write up a certificate of dismissal and then divorce her."
Jesus explained, "Moses only wrote that command because you guys are so stubborn and hardhearted. But way back when God first created everything, he made male and female to be together."
"Because of this, a man leaves his dad and mom, and when he gets married, he becomes one flesh with his wife. They're not two separate people anymore, but they form a brand-new unity."
"Since God created this super close union between the two sexes, no one should mess with his artwork by trying to cut them apart."
Later, when they were back home, the disciples brought the topic up again. Jesus gave it to them straight:

"If a man divorces his wife just so he can go marry someone else, he's basically cheating on her (committing adultery). And if a woman divorces her husband to marry someone else, she's also committing adultery."
People started bringing their kids to Jesus, hoping he'd touch them. But the disciples tried to shoo them away.

Jesus got totally fired up and let them know it! "Don't push these children away! Don't you ever get between them and me! These kids are right at the heart of what life in God's kingdom is all about."
"Listen up: Unless you accept God's kingdom with the simple trust of a child, you'll never get in." Then, he gathered the children into his arms and laid his hands on them, blessing each one.
§ To Enter God's Kingdom
As Jesus was walking out into the street, a guy came running up to him. He greeted Jesus with a lot of respect and asked, "Good Teacher, what do I need to do to get eternal life?"

Jesus replied, "Why are you calling me good? Nobody is truly good except God himself. You know the commandments, right? Don't murder, don't cheat on your spouse, don't steal, don't lie, don't rip people off, and honor your father and mother."
The guy said, "Teacher, I've kept all those rules since I was a kid!"

Jesus looked him right in the eye—and loved him! He said, "There's just one more thing you need to do: Go sell everything you own and give the money to the poor. All that wealth will then be like treasure stored up in heaven. And then, come follow me."
The man's face totally clouded over. This was the last thing he expected to hear, and he walked off with a really heavy heart. He was holding onto a lot of stuff, and he wasn't about to let it go.
Jesus looked at his disciples and said, "Do you have any idea how incredibly hard it is for people who 'have it all' to enter God's kingdom?"

The disciples couldn't believe what they were hearing, but Jesus kept going: "You seriously can't imagine how difficult. I'd say it's easier for a camel to squeeze through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to get into God's kingdom."
That really got their attention. "Then who even has a chance at all?" they asked.
Jesus was blunt: "No chance at all if you think you can pull it off by yourself. But you have every single chance in the world if you let God do it."
Peter tried a different approach. "Hey, we left everything behind and followed you."
Jesus said, "Mark my words, anyone who gives up their house, brothers, sisters, mom, dad, children, land—whatever—because of me and the Good News (the Message) won't lose out."
"They'll get it all back, but multiplied many times over in homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and land—though there will be troubles too. And then, the awesome bonus of eternal life!"
"This is another one of those Great Reversals: Many who are first now will end up last, and the last will end up first."
Back on the road, they set out for Jerusalem. Jesus was walking ahead of them, and they were following, confused and a little bit scared.

He pulled the Twelve aside and started explaining again what was going to happen next. "Listen to me carefully. We're heading up to Jerusalem. When we get there, the Son of Man will be betrayed to the religious leaders and scholars.
"They will sentence him to death. Then they'll hand him over to the Romans, who will mock him, spit on him, give him the third degree, and kill him. But after three days, he will rise alive."
§ The Highest Places of Honor
James and John, Zebedee's sons, came up to him. "Teacher, we have something we really want you to do for us."
"What is it? I'll see what I can do," Jesus responded.
"Arrange it," they said, "so that we'll get the absolute highest places of honor in your glory—one of us at your right side, the other at your left."
Jesus said, "You have no idea what you're even asking for. Are you capable of drinking the cup I drink, or being baptized in the baptism I'm about to be plunged into?"
"Sure," they said. "Why not?"

Jesus told them, "You know what? You actually will drink the cup I drink and be baptized in my baptism. But as for giving out those places of honor, that's not my decision to make. There are other arrangements for that."
When the other ten disciples heard about this conversation, they totally lost their cool with James and John.

Jesus called them all together to calm things down. "You've seen how godless rulers throw their weight around," he said, "and how quickly power goes to people's heads when they get a little bit of it."
"It's not going to be like that among you. Whoever wants to be truly great must become a servant to everyone else. And whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave."
"That's exactly what the Son of Man has done: He didn't come to be served, but to serve others—and then to give away his life as a ransom for many."
They spent some time in Jericho. As Jesus was leaving town, trailed by his disciples and a huge parade of people, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus (son of Timaeus) was sitting by the side of the road.
When he heard that Jesus the Nazarene was passing by, he started screaming, "Son of David, Jesus! Have mercy, have mercy on me!"
Lots of people tried to shut him up, but he just yelled even louder, "Son of David! Have mercy, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped dead in his tracks. "Call him over," he said.
So they called to the blind man. "It's your lucky day! Get up! He's calling you to come!" Throwing off his coat, he jumped to his feet at once and came to Jesus.
Jesus asked him, "What can I do for you?"
The blind man said, "Rabbi (Teacher), I want to see!"
"You're all set," said Jesus. "Your faith has saved and healed you." In that very instant, he got his sight back and followed Jesus down the road.

title: The Parade and the Temple Takedown
paragraphs: § Entering Jerusalem on a Colt
Getting close to Jerusalem, near Bethphage and Bethany on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two of his disciples ahead with a mission.

He told them, "Head over to the village you see straight across from you. The second you get there, you'll spot a young colt tied up, one that's never been ridden before. Go untie it and bring it here."
"And if anyone asks, 'Hey, what do you think you're doing?' just tell them, 'The Master needs it, and he'll send it right back after he's used it.'"
So, the disciples went off and, sure enough, found the colt tied right by a door on the street corner. They started untying it.
Then, some people standing around there were like, "Whoa, what are you guys doing untying that colt?"

The disciples answered them exactly the way Jesus had told them to, and the people backed off, leaving them alone. They brought the colt to Jesus, threw their jackets over its back, and Jesus hopped on.
The crowd totally went wild, giving him an amazing welcome! Some people were throwing their coats on the street, while others were spreading out rushes they'd cut from the fields.
People were running ahead and following behind, shouting at the top of their lungs:
"Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in God's name! Blessed is the coming kingdom of our ancestor David! Hosanna in the highest heaven!"

Jesus entered Jerusalem, then went straight into the Temple. He took a good look around, checking everything out. But by then it was getting late, so he went back to Bethany with the twelve disciples.
§ The Cursed Fig Tree
The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus felt super hungry. He spotted a fig tree in the distance, covered in leaves.
He walked up to it, hoping to find some figs for breakfast, but all he found were leaves. (It wasn't even the season for figs yet.) He spoke directly to the tree:
"No one is ever going to eat fruit from you again—ever!" And his disciples definitely heard him say it.

They arrived in Jerusalem. As soon as Jesus walked into the Temple, he immediately started kicking out everyone who had set up shop there, buying and selling stuff. He flipped over the tables of the money changers (bankers) and knocked over the stalls of the guys selling pigeons.
He wouldn't even let anyone carry a basket through the Temple area. Then he started teaching them, quoting from the Scriptures:
"My house was meant to be a house of prayer for all nations; but you guys have turned it into a hangout for thieves!"

The high priests and the religious scholars heard all this going down and immediately started plotting how they could get rid of him. They were seriously rattled, because the whole crowd was totally captivated by his teaching.
That evening, Jesus and his disciples left the city.
The next morning, as they were walking along the road, they saw the fig tree. It was completely shriveled up, like a dry stick.
Peter, remembering what Jesus had said the day before, pointed it out to him: "Rabbi, look! That fig tree you cursed is all shriveled up!"

Jesus responded in a really straightforward way: "Really embrace this God-life. Seriously, embrace it, and nothing will be too much for you. Take this mountain, for example: Just say, 'Go jump in the lake'—no hesitating or humming and hawing—and it's as good as done.
"That's why I'm telling you to pray for absolutely everything, from the smallest thing to the biggest. Include everything as you embrace this God-life, and you'll get God's everything."

"And when you get into the posture of prayer, remember that it's not just about asking. If you have anything against someone, forgive them—only then will your heavenly Father be willing to wipe your slate clean of your own sins too."
§ His Credentials

Later, when they were back in Jerusalem again, walking through the Temple, the high priests, religious scholars, and leaders came up to him and demanded, "Show us your credentials. Who gave you the authority to speak and act like this?"
Jesus shot back, "First, let me ask you a question. Answer my question, and then I'll show you my credentials. About John's baptism—who authorized it: heaven or humans? Tell me."

They were totally put on the spot and knew it. They huddled together and whispered, "If we say 'heaven,' he'll ask us why we didn't believe John. But if we say 'humans,' we'll have a huge problem with the people because they all see John as a prophet."
So they decided to just give up that round to Jesus. "We don't know," they said.
Jesus replied, "Then I won't answer your question either."

title: Traps, Taxes, and the Ultimate Rule
paragraphs: § The Story About a Vineyard

Then Jesus started dropping some stories on them. He was like, "Okay, so this guy plants a vineyard. He puts up a fence, digs out a winepress (where they'd stomp grapes for wine), builds a watchtower, then hands it over to some farmhands and goes on a trip. When harvest time came around, he sent a servant back to the farmhands to collect his share of the profits."

But get this – the farmhands grabbed the servant, beat him up, and sent him back with nothing. So the owner sent another servant. That one they tarred and feathered—a really humiliating punishment back then. Then he sent another, and they just straight-up killed him. It kept going like that with a bunch of other servants. Some they beat up, some they flat-out murdered.
Finally, there was only one person left: his super loved son. In one last desperate attempt, he sent him, thinking, 'Surely, they'll show some respect for my son.'

But those greedy farmhands saw their opportunity. They practically rubbed their hands together, saying, 'Whoa, this is the guy who's gonna inherit everything! Let's kill him and then it'll all be ours!' So they grabbed him, killed him, and tossed his body right over the fence.

So, Jesus asked, "What do you guys think the owner of the vineyard will do?" He answered his own question: "Right. He'll come back, get rid of everyone responsible, and then give the vineyard to other people to take care of. You can even read about it in the Bible, it says:
‘That stone the builders tossed aside has become the most important stone, the cornerstone! This is totally God’s doing; we can barely believe our eyes—it’s that amazing!’"

The religious leaders wanted to totally jump him right then and there. But they were kinda scared of what the general public would think, so they held back. They knew the story was clearly about them. So, they got out of there as fast as they could.
§ Paying Taxes to Caesar

After that, some Pharisees and followers of Herod sent people to try and trap Jesus. They hoped to catch him saying something that would get him in trouble. They came up to him and said, "Teacher, we know you're legit. You're honest, you don't care what other people think, you don't just tell your students what they want to hear, and you teach God's truth accurately. So, tell us: Is it legal to pay taxes to Caesar (the Roman emperor) or not?"
Jesus knew instantly it was a trick question. He said, "Why are you trying to play these games with me? Bring me a coin so I can look at it."
They handed him a denarius (a Roman coin). He asked, "Whose picture is this on the coin? And whose name is written on it?"
"Caesar's," they replied.
Jesus then said, "Well, then, give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give God what belongs to God." Their jaws dropped. They were totally speechless.
§ Our Intimacies Will Be with God

Next, some Sadducees showed up. These guys were a religious group who didn't believe in the resurrection (coming back from the dead). They asked, "Teacher, Moses wrote that if a man dies and leaves a wife but no kids, his brother has to marry the widow and have children with her to continue the family name. Okay, so imagine there were seven brothers. The first one got married, but then died without any kids. The second brother married her. He died, still no kids. Same thing with the third. All seven brothers took turns, but none of them had children with her. Finally, the wife died too."
"So, when everyone is raised from the dead at the resurrection, whose wife will she be? All seven of them were her husband!"

Jesus said, "You guys are way off base, and here's why: First, you don't really understand what God has said. Second, you don't understand how God actually works. After people are raised from the dead, marriage isn't a thing anymore. It'll be just like with angels now—all our deepest joys and closest connections then will be directly with God."

"And about the dead, and whether or not they're even raised up—haven't you ever read the Bible? Like how God spoke to Moses at the burning bush and said, 'I *am*—not *was*—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? The living God is the God of the living, not the dead. You are way, way off base."
§ The Most Important Commandment

One of the religion scholars came over. He'd been listening to all the intense back-and-forth questions and answers and could tell how incredibly smart Jesus was with his responses. So, he decided to ask his own question: "Which of all the commandments is the most important one?"

Jesus replied, "The most important one is this: 'Listen up, Israel: The Lord your God is one and only; so love the Lord God with absolutely everything you've got—all your passion, all your prayer, all your intelligence, and all your energy.' And here's the second one, just as important: 'Love other people just as much as you love yourself.' There isn't any other commandment that even comes close to these two."

The religion scholar responded, "Wow, Teacher! That's a fantastic answer! So clear and spot-on—that God is one and there's no other. And loving him with all your passion, intelligence, and energy, and loving others as much as you love yourself. Seriously, that's way better than all the offerings and sacrifices put together!"
When Jesus saw how sharp and insightful the scholar was, he told him, "You're almost there, right on the edge of God's kingdom." After that, nobody dared to ask him another question.
While he was teaching in the Temple, Jesus asked, "How come the religion scholars claim that the Messiah is David's 'son,' when we all know that David, inspired by the Holy Spirit, said:
‘God said to my Master, “Sit here at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.”’
Here, David calls the Messiah 'my Master'—so how can the Messiah also be his 'son'?"
The huge crowd was totally thrilled with what they heard.

He kept on teaching. "Watch out for those religion scholars! They love strutting around in their fancy robes, soaking up all the public praise, grabbing the best seats, and always sitting at the head table at every church event. And all the while, they're actually taking advantage of people who are weak and helpless. The longer they make their prayers, the worse they get. But they're going to pay for it in the end."

Jesus sat down across from the offering box (the collection plate) and watched how everyone was putting money in. Lots of rich people were dropping in big bucks. Then, one poor widow came up and put in two tiny coins—like, a measly two cents.

Jesus called his disciples over and said, "Listen up, because this is the truth: This poor widow actually gave more to the collection than everyone else combined. All the others gave what they won't even miss; but she gave way more than she could afford—she gave literally everything she had."

title: The End of the World Survival Guide
paragraphs: § Doomsday Deceivers
As Jesus was walking away from the Temple, one of his disciples pointed and said, "Teacher, seriously, check out that stonework! Those massive buildings!"

Jesus replied, "You're really impressed by all this fancy architecture, huh? Well, guess what? Not a single stone in this whole place is going to be left standing. It's all gonna end up in a huge pile of rubble."

Later, Jesus was chilling on Mount Olives, with a perfect view of the Temple. Peter, James, John, and Andrew pulled him aside and asked, "Spill it, when is all this going to happen? What kind of sign should we look for that things are totally coming to a head?"

Jesus started by saying, "Listen up, watch out for people who try to trick you with 'doomsday' prophecies. A lot of leaders are going to pop up with fake identities, claiming, 'I'm the One.' They'll fool a ton of people.

When you start hearing about wars and rumors of wars, don't lose your cool and don't panic. That's just how history goes, it's routine, and it's not a sign that the end is here yet. Nations will fight nations, and rulers will fight rulers, over and over again. There will be earthquakes in different places, and famines.
But honestly, all those things are nothing compared to the really intense stuff that's still coming."

"And seriously, heads up! They're going to drag you into court. And then things will go from bad to worse, like a total dog-eat-dog situation, with everyone coming after you just because you're associated with my name.
But you're put in those situations to be like watchmen for the truth. The Message (the Good News about me) has to be preached all over the world."

"When they bring you into court after you've been betrayed, don't stress about what you're going to say. When the time comes, just speak what's genuinely on your heart—the Holy Spirit will actually speak through you and make his witness."
"It's going to get so bad that brother will kill brother, fathers will kill their children, and children will even kill their parents. There's no telling who will hate you because of me.
But you gotta stick with it—that's what's required. Hang in there until the very end. You won't regret it; you'll be saved."
§ Run for the Hills
"But get ready to bolt when you see 'the monster of desecration' set up where it should never be. If you're reading this, make sure you understand what I'm talking about."

"If you're living in Judea at that time, run for the hills! If you're working in the yard, don't even go back to the house to grab anything. If you're out in the field, don't go back to get your coat.
Pregnant and nursing mothers are going to have an especially hard time. Hope and pray that this doesn't happen in the middle of winter."
"These are going to be incredibly tough days—nothing like it has ever happened from the moment God created the world right up until now. And there will never be anything like it again.
If he just let those days of trouble play out, no one would survive. But because of God's chosen people, the ones he personally picked, he has already stepped in to shorten that time."
§ No One Knows the Day or Hour
"If anyone tries to get your attention, yelling, 'Hey, here's the Messiah!' or points, 'There he is!'—don't fall for it. Fake Messiahs and lying preachers are going to pop up everywhere.
Their impressive credentials and their mind-blowing performances will totally trick even those who should know better. So watch out. I'm giving you a heads-up now."
"After those hard times, the sun will start to fade out, the moon will get cloudy, stars will fall out of the sky, and even the cosmic powers will tremble."

"And then, everyone will see the Son of Man arrive in a super grand way, his coming filling the sky—no one will miss it! He'll send out the angels; they will gather his chosen people from all four directions, from one end of the earth to the other."
"Learn a lesson from the fig tree. The moment you notice its buds forming, that first tiny hint of green, you know summer is just around the corner.
And it's the same with you. When you see all these things I've described, you'll know he is right at the door. Don't take this lightly.
I'm not just saying this for some generation way in the future, but for this one, too—these things will actually happen. The sky and earth will eventually wear out; but my words won't ever wear out."
"But the exact day and hour? No one knows that—not even the angels in heaven, not even the Son. Only the Father knows. So stay super alert, because you don't know the exact schedule.
It's like a guy who goes on a trip, leaves his house, and puts his servants in charge. Each one gets a task, and he tells the gatekeeper to stay awake and watch.
So, stay at your post, watching. You have no idea when the homeowner is coming back, whether it's evening, midnight, when the rooster crows, or in the morning.
You don't want him showing up unexpectedly and finding you asleep on the job. I'm saying it to you, and I'm saying it to everyone: Stay at your post. Keep watch."

title: The Perfume, the Passover, and the Ultimate Betrayal
paragraphs: § Anointing His Head

Just two days until the eight-day Passover Festival and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The head priests and religious experts were secretly trying to figure out how to grab Jesus and kill him. They decided it couldn't happen during Passover Week though. "We don't want to stir up the crowds," they said.
Jesus was in Bethany, staying at Simon the Leper's house. While they were all eating dinner, a woman showed up with a bottle of super expensive perfume.
She opened it up and poured it right on his head! Some of the other guests got totally ticked off about it. "That's messed up! What a complete waste!" they grumbled.
"This perfume could've easily been sold for way more than a year's salary, and the money given to the poor!" They were absolutely fuming, practically exploding with anger over what she did.
But Jesus said, "Leave her alone. Why are you giving her such a hard time? She just did something incredibly meaningful for me."
"You'll always have poor people with you for the rest of your lives. Whenever you feel like it, you can do something for them. But it's not like that with me."

"She did what she could when she could—she basically prepared my body for burial ahead of time. And you can be sure that wherever this Message is preached anywhere in the whole world, what she just did is going to be talked about with admiration."
Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve main followers, went to the secret meeting of the head priests, totally determined to betray Jesus. They couldn't believe their luck, and promised to pay him well.
He started looking for just the right moment to hand Jesus over.
§ Traitor to the Son of Man

On the first of the Days of Unleavened Bread (which was the day they traditionally prepared the Passover sacrifice), his disciples asked him, "Where do you want us to go and get things ready so you can eat the Passover meal?"

He sent two of his disciples, saying, "Go into the city. A man carrying a water jug will meet you. Follow him. Ask the owner of whichever house he enters, 'The Teacher wants to know, where is my guest room where I can eat the Passover meal with my disciples?'"
"He will show you a big room upstairs, already cleaned up and ready. Get things prepared for us there."
The disciples left, went into the city, found everything exactly as he had told them, and got the Passover meal ready.

After sunset, he came with the twelve. As they were at the supper table eating, Jesus said, "I have something tough but important to tell you: One of you is going to hand me over to the people who want to hurt me, one who is eating with me right now."
They were shocked, and started asking, one after another, "It's not me, is it?"

He said, "It's one of the Twelve, someone who dips his bread in the same bowl with me. In one way, it totally makes sense that the Son of Man is going through this betrayal, just like the Scriptures said—no surprises there."
"But in another way, the guy who turns him in, who betrays the Son of Man—it would be better for him if he had never even been born!"
§ "This Is My Body"
During their meal, he took some bread, blessed it, broke it into pieces, and gave it to them. Then he said, "Take this, it is my body."
Then he took the cup (chalice), thanked God, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it. He said, "This is my blood, God's new covenant, poured out for many people."
"I won't be drinking wine again until that new day when I drink it in the kingdom of God."
They sang a hymn (a religious song) and then went straight to Mount Olives.
Jesus told them, "You're all going to feel like your world is falling apart and that it's my fault. There's a Scripture that says, 'I will strike the shepherd; the sheep will scatter.'"
"But after I am raised up, I will go ahead of you, leading the way to Galilee."
Peter blurted out, "Even if everyone else is ashamed of you when things go completely wrong, I won't be!"
Jesus said, "Don't be so sure. Today, actually this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny knowing me three times."
Peter protested loudly, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never deny you!" All the others said the same thing.
§ Gethsemane
They came to an area called Gethsemane. Jesus told his disciples, "Sit here while I pray." He took Peter, James, and John with him. He felt like he was sinking into a suffocating, dark pit.
He told them, "I feel so bad right now, I could die. Stay here and keep watch with me."

Going a little ahead, he fell to the ground and prayed for a way out: "Papa, Father, you can—can't you?—get me out of this. Take this cup away from me. But please, don't do what I want—do what you want."
He came back and found them totally asleep. He said to Peter, "Simon, you went to sleep on me? Can't you stay awake with me for just one hour?"

"Stay alert, keep praying, so you don't walk into a dangerous situation without even realizing it. Don't be naive. Part of you is super eager, ready for anything for God; but another part is as lazy as an old dog sleeping by the fire."
He then went back and prayed the exact same prayer. Returning, he again found them sound asleep. They just couldn't keep their eyes open, and they didn't have a good excuse.

He came back a third time and said, "Are you going to sleep all night? No—you've slept long enough. Time's up. The Son of Man is about to be betrayed into the hands of sinners. Get up. Let's get going. My betrayer has arrived."
§ A Bunch of Thugs

No sooner were the words out of his mouth when Judas, the one from the Twelve, showed up. And with him was a bunch of thugs, sent by the head priests, religious experts, and leaders, all carrying swords and clubs.
The betrayer had set up a signal with them: "The one I kiss, that's him—grab him. Make sure he doesn't get away." He went straight to Jesus and said, "Rabbi!" and kissed him.
The others then grabbed Jesus and roughed him up. One of the men standing there pulled out his sword, swung, and chopped off the Chief Priest's servant's ear.

Jesus said to them, "What is this, coming after me with swords and clubs as if I were some dangerous criminal? Day after day I've been sitting in the Temple teaching, and you never even tried to lay a hand on me."
"What you've actually done is confirm what the prophetic writings said would happen." All the disciples ditched him and ran away.
A young man was following along, and all he had on was a bedsheet. Some of the men grabbed him but he got away, running off naked, leaving them holding the sheet.
§ Condemned to Death

They led Jesus to the Chief Priest, where the head priests, religious leaders, and scholars had all gathered together. Peter followed at a safe distance until they got to the Chief Priest's courtyard, where he blended in with the servants and warmed himself by the fire.

The head priests, working with the Jewish Council, searched high and low for evidence against Jesus that they could use to sentence him to death. They found nothing. Lots of people were willing to make up false charges, but nothing made sense, and their stories ended up canceling each other out.

Then a few of them stood up and lied: "We heard him say, 'I'm going to tear down this Temple, built by hard work, and in three days build another one without lifting a hand.'" But even they couldn't agree on the exact details.
In the middle of all this, the Chief Priest stood up and asked Jesus, "What do you have to say to these accusations?" Jesus was silent. He didn't say anything.
The Chief Priest tried again, this time asking, "Are you the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One?"
Jesus said, "Yes, I am, and you'll see it yourself: The Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Mighty One, arriving on the clouds of heaven."

The Chief Priest totally lost his temper. Ripping his clothes, he yelled, "Did you hear that? After that, do we need any more witnesses? You heard the blasphemy (insulting God)! Are you going to stand for it?"
They condemned him, every single one of them. The sentence: death.
Some of them started spitting at him. They blindfolded his eyes, then hit him, saying, "Who hit you? Prophesy!" The guards, punching and slapping, took him away.
§ The Rooster Crowed

While all this was going on, Peter was down in the courtyard. One of the Chief Priest's servant girls came in and, seeing Peter warming himself there, looked hard at him and said, "You were with that guy from Nazareth, Jesus."
He denied it: "I don't know what you're talking about." He went out on the porch. A rooster crowed.
The girl spotted him again and started telling the people standing around, "He's one of them." He denied it again.
After a little while, the bystanders brought it up again. "You've gotta be one of them. You've got 'Galilean' written all over you."

Now Peter got really nervous and swore, "I never even saw this man you're talking about!" Just then the rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered how Jesus had said, "Before a rooster crows twice, you'll deny me three times." He completely broke down in tears.
