title: The Trial, the Torture, and the Cross
paragraphs: § Standing Before Pilate

First thing in the morning, as soon as the sun came up, the head priests, along with the religious leaders and the experts in Jewish law (scholars), got together for a big meeting with the whole Jewish Council. After they tied Jesus up really tight, they dragged him out and handed him over to Pilate.
Pilate asked Jesus, "So, are you really the 'King of the Jews'?" Jesus just replied, "If you say so." Meanwhile, the head priests started throwing a ton of accusations at him, one after another.

Pilate tried again, "Seriously, aren't you going to say anything? That's a pretty long list of stuff they're accusing you of." But Jesus stayed totally silent. Pilate was actually pretty blown away by that, super impressed.

During the annual festival (Passover), it was a tradition to let one prisoner go free, whoever the crowd picked. At that time, there was this guy named Barabbas, who was locked up with some rebels (insurrectionists) who had actually committed murder during a riot against the Roman government.

When the crowd showed up, ready to ask for a prisoner to be released, Pilate got ahead of them. He asked, "Do you want me to release the King of the Jews for you?" Pilate totally knew by then that the head priests had only turned Jesus over to him out of pure hatred and jealousy.

But the head priests had already worked up the crowd, getting them all hyped up to ask for Barabbas to be released instead. Pilate tried again, "So, what am I supposed to do with this guy you call the King of the Jews?"
They screamed, "Nail him to a cross!"
Pilate pushed back, "But for what crime? What did he even do wrong?" But they just yelled even louder, "Nail him to a cross!"
So, Pilate gave the crowd exactly what they wanted. He set Barabbas free and then handed Jesus over to be whipped and crucified.

The soldiers took Jesus inside the palace (which was called the Praetorium) and called the entire army unit (brigade) together. They dressed him up in a purple robe and put a crown made of thorny branches on his head. Then they started making fun of him, yelling, "Awesome, King of the Jews!"

They kept hitting him on the head with a stick, spitting on him, and kneeling down to pretend to worship him. After they'd had their fun, they ripped off the purple cape and put his own clothes back on him. Then they marched him out to nail him to the cross.
§ The Crucifixion
There was a guy just walking by, coming in from work. His name was Simon from Cyrene, and he was the dad of Alexander and Rufus. The soldiers forced him to carry Jesus' cross.

The soldiers brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which literally means "Skull Hill." They offered him a mild painkiller—wine mixed with myrrh (a bitter resin)—but he wouldn't take it. And then they nailed him to the cross.
They divided up his clothes and threw dice to see who would get them.

They nailed him up at nine o'clock in the morning. The charge against him—"THE KING OF THE JEWS"—was scribbled on a sign above his head. Along with him, they crucified two criminals, one on his right side and one on his left.

People passing by on the road kept jeering at him, shaking their heads as if they were sad, but really just making fun: "Hey, you bragged that you could tear down the Temple and then rebuild it in three days—so prove it! Save yourself! If you're actually God's Son, then come down from that cross!"

The head priests, along with the religious scholars, were right there in the crowd, having a blast making fun of him too: "He saved other people—but he can't even save himself! So, he's the Messiah, huh? The King of Israel? Then let him climb down from that cross right now. We'll all become believers then!" Even the guys who were being crucified next to him joined in the mockery.

At noon, the sky suddenly went completely dark. The darkness lasted for three hours. At three o'clock, Jesus groaned from deep inside, crying out loudly, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?" which means, "My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?"

Some of the people standing nearby who heard him said, "Listen, he's calling for Elijah." Someone quickly ran off, soaked a sponge in sour wine, put it on a stick, and held it up for him to drink, saying, "Let's see if Elijah actually comes to take him down."

But Jesus, with one last loud cry, took his final breath. At that exact moment, the huge curtain in the Temple ripped right down the middle. When the Roman captain who was standing guard right in front of him saw that Jesus had stopped breathing, he said, "This guy absolutely had to be the Son of God!"
§ Taken to a Tomb

There were some women watching from a distance, including Mary Magdalene, Mary (who was the mother of the younger James and Joses), and Salome. When Jesus was in Galilee, these women had followed him and served him, and they had come up to Jerusalem with him.

Later that afternoon, since it was the Day of Preparation (which means the day before the Sabbath, or Saturday), Joseph of Arimathea arrived. He was a highly respected member of the Jewish Council and was someone who eagerly looked forward to God's kingdom.

Gathering up his courage, he went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body. Pilate was surprised, wondering if Jesus could really be dead so quickly, so he called for the captain to confirm that he was actually dead. Once the captain assured him, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.

Joseph had already bought a linen shroud (a burial cloth). He took Jesus down from the cross, wrapped him in the shroud, placed him in a tomb that had been carved into the rock, and then rolled a large stone across the opening to seal it. Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, watched the burial.

title: The Empty Tomb and the Ultimate Comeback
paragraphs: § The Resurrection

After the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices to anoint Jesus's body. Very early on Sunday morning, as the sun was rising, they went to the tomb, wondering, "Who is going to help us roll that massive stone away?"

But when they got there, the stone was already rolled back — and it was a huge stone! They walked right into the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed all in white. They were completely taken aback, totally stunned.

He said, "Don't be afraid. I know you're looking for Jesus of Nazareth, the one they nailed to the cross. He's been raised up — he's not here anymore! See for yourselves, the place is empty. Now get going: tell his disciples, and Peter, that he's going ahead of you to Galilee. You'll see him there, exactly like he said."
The women ran out of the tomb as fast as they could, totally freaked out, their heads spinning. They were so stunned they didn't say a word to anyone.

[Heads up: the oldest copies of Mark end at verse 8 — the rest (verses 9-20) comes from later copies. Here's how that longer ending tells it:] After rising from the dead, Jesus appeared early on Sunday morning, first to Mary Magdalene — the same Mary he had freed from seven demons. She ran to his heartbroken friends, who were weeping and carrying on, and told them the news. But when they heard she had seen him alive and well, they didn't believe her one bit.
Later, he appeared in a totally different form to two of them as they were walking out in the countryside. They rushed back and told the rest, but no one believed them either.

Still later, he appeared to the Eleven themselves while they were eating supper — and he called them out hard for their stubborn refusal to believe the people who had seen him risen. Then he said, "Go into the entire world and preach God's Good News to absolutely everyone. Anyone who believes and is baptized will be saved — but anyone who refuses to believe will be condemned."

"And these amazing signs will follow everyone who believes: they'll drive out demons in my name, they'll speak in brand-new languages, they'll pick up snakes, they'll drink poison and walk away totally fine, and they'll lay hands on sick people and heal them."

After briefing them, the Master Jesus was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God, the place of honor. The disciples went out and preached everywhere, and the Master worked right alongside them, backing up the message with undeniable miracles. (Note: Mark 16:9-20 — the part in brackets — isn't found in the earliest handwritten copies of Mark.)
